t:
Section 201 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, as amended, is amended by—

    (a) 
inserting “(except a new animal drug or an animal feed bearing or containing a new animal drug)” after “Any drug” in subparagraph (1) of paragraph (p);
 
    (b) 
inserting “(except a new animal drug or an animal feed bearing or containing a new animal drug)” after “Any drug” in subparagraph (2) of paragraph (p);
 
    (c) 
striking out the period at the end of subparagraph (4) of paragraph (s) and inserting in lieu thereof “; or”, and by adding a new subparagraph (5) to read as follows: “(5) a new animal drug.”:
 
    (d) 
inserting“. 512,”after “409” in paragraph (u); and
 
    (e) 
adding at the end of such section the following new paragraphs:


“(w) 
The term ‘new animal drug’ means any drug intended for use for animals other than man, including any drug intended for use hi animal feed but not including such animal feed,—

“(1) 
the composition of which is such that such drug is not generally recognized, among experts qualified by scientific training and experience to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of animal drugs, as safe and effective for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the labeling thereof; except that such a drug not so recognized shall not be deemed to be a ‘new animal drug’ if at any time prior to June 25, 1938, it was subject to the Food and Drug Act of June 30, 1936, as amended, and if at such time its labeling contained the same representations concerning the conditions of its use; or


“(2) 
the composition of which is such that such drug, as a result of investigations to determine its safety and effectiveness for use under such conditions, has become so recognized but which has not, otherwise than in such investigations, been used to a material extent or for a material time under such conditions; or


“(3) 
which drug is composed wholly or partly of any kind of penicillin, streptomycin, chlortetracycline, chloramphenicol, or bacitracin, or any derivative thereof, except when there is in effect a published order of the Secretary declaring such drug not to be a new animal drug on the grounds that (A) the requirement of certification of batches of such drug, as provided for in section 512(n), is not necessary to insure that the objectives specified in paragraph (3) thereof are achieved and (B) that neither subparagraph (1) nor (2) of this paragraph (w) applies to such drug.



“(x) 
The term ‘animal feed’, as used in paragraph (w) of this section, in section 512, and in provisions of this Act referring to such paragraph or section, means an article which is intended for use for food for animals other than man and which is intended for use as a substantial source of nutrients in the diet of the animal, and is not limited to a mixture intended to be the sole ration of the animal.”

fable.w: The section only amends definitions in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, adding the terms 'new animal drug' and 'animal feed'. The tempting reading is that the reference to 'experts' signals outside consultation, but it is a substantive definitional standard (general recognition of safety), not a process in which the government consults outsiders before a decision. The mention of a 'published order of the Secretary' is an exception to the definition and does not establish a comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: is not generally recognized, among experts qualified by scientific training and experience to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of animal drugs, as safe and effective

qwen_block.w: This section defines the term 'new animal drug' by referencing the general recognition of safety and effectiveness among qualified experts. It does not establish a process for the government to consult with or coordinate with these experts before making a decision; rather, it uses their collective scientific consensus as a static criterion for classification. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or consultation requirement imposed on the agency.
qwen_block.s: the composition of which is such that such drug is not generally recognized, among experts qualified by scientific training and experience to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of animal drugs, as safe and effective for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the labeling thereof

opus.w: This section only amends definitions in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act ('new animal drug' and 'animal feed'). The mention of experts sets a standard of general scientific recognition. It does not require the government to consult outside experts before deciding anything. The 'published order of the Secretary' is a one-sided declaration by the Secretary, with no comment period, hearing, or other step that brings in people outside the federal government.
opus.s: is not generally recognized, among experts qualified by scientific training and experience to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of animal drugs, as safe and effective
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the phrase "experts qualified by scientific training and experience" means outside experts are consulted, or that a "published order of the Secretary" amounts to rulemaking. Neither holds up. The experts phrase only sets the "generally recognized as safe and effective" test inside a definition; no step requires the agency to consult anyone outside the government. The published order is a declaration by the Secretary alone. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section provides statutory definitions for terms like 'new animal drug' and 'animal feed'. While the definition of 'new animal drug' references recognition 'among experts,' this describes a condition of general scientific consensus rather than a procedural requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a decision. There is no advisory board, comment period, or consultation process mandated in this text.
qwen_chat.s: the composition of which is such that such drug is not generally recognized, among experts qualified by scientific training and experience to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of animal drugs, as safe and effective for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the labeling thereof
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the definition of "new animal drug" relies on recognition "among experts qualified by scientific training and experience," which implies a consultation with outside experts. However, this is a statutory definition of a term based on a general state of knowledge or consensus, not a procedural requirement for the agency to consult with specific outside parties before making a decision. There is no mechanism described for the agency to seek input from these experts; rather, the status of the drug is determined by whether it *is* generally recognized.
